ruling.recommended_action: Route to Ryde trust & safety: review the rider's threatening message (F4) against the recorded chat, and apply SAFE-1 account measures against the rider if the threat is confirmed; advise the driver of the RydeHELP reporting path and 995 for any medical or safety need.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a driver-filed safety case. The trip itself is uncontested: actual distance 8.5 km exactly equals the optimal route 8.5 km, +0.0 km (-1%), and duration 13.2 min is shorter than the 16.3 min estimate [F1][F2], so no off-route segment exists and no route-deviation refund can arise under RD-1/RD-2. The metered charge of $20.75 is not in dispute in any fee-claim sense here, and no cancellation or waiting fee is at issue, so NS-0 through NS-7 are not engaged.

The safety screen is decisive. The chat record contains two messages, both timestamped [F5]: the driver's 18:24 request "Please do not smoke in the car" [F3] and the rider's 18:24 reply "Say that again and I will punch you" [F4]. Read in context — a direct, conditional threat of physical violence aimed at the driver in response to a lawful in-car request — this is intimidation and abuse of a party, which Ryde's code of conduct bars as "abuse of any kind" [RD-1 not applicable here; SAFE-1]. The driver's written statement corroborates the same exchange, that he raised the smoking request politely, received the threat, and kept driving without answering; the driver himself reports it as a safety incident [F6]. My finding is therefore "confirmed" rather than merely suspected, on the plain words of the rider's own message [F4].

Because a safety incident under SAFE-1 is present, the policy removes the case from automatic adjudication: the correct outcome is escalate, with a factual summary for a human reviewer rather than any ruling on money [SAFE-1]. Were this a driving-injury matter, SAFE-2 would also require escalation with the 995 / commercial-insurance / RydeHELP reporting paths; the record shows no accident or injury allegation, so I do not rely on it. Nothing in the profiles decides anything: the rider's 735-day account, 4.5 rating and zero upheld disputes [F7], and the driver's 1974-day account, 4.82 rating and 743 trips with no disputes [F8] are context for the reviewer only and cannot by themselves establish or defeat any claim.

The evidence on the disputed element is complete: the full chat is imported and every message carries a timestamp [F5], so the threat and its timing are settled, not undetermined, and no clause needs a record that is missing. The escalation is grounded in the safety clause itself, not in an evidence gap. On the money: no refund formula applies, because no unprotected off-route segment exists [F1] and the trace allows escalate as the only outcome [SAFE-1]; amount is therefore null. I record no account action myself — Ryde retains that decision, and the recommended action asks its safety team to consider one against the rider under SAFE-1.
ruling.escalation_reason: Driver-filed safety incident on a completed RydeTAXI trip (Tampines Mall → Changi Airport T3, pickup 18:15, drop-off 18:28). At 18:24 the driver messaged the rider not to smoke in the car [F3]; at the same minute the rider replied, in the timestamped chat, "Say that again and I will punch you" [F4][F5]; the driver's post-trip statement repeats the exchange and says he kept driving without replying [F6]. Disputed element: whether the rider committed an act of intimidation/abuse against the driver — the judge reads the words as a confirmed threat. No alleged off-route driving (8.5 km actual vs 8.5 km optimal [F1]), so the only open question is the rider account action under SAFE-1; reviewer to check F3, F4, F5, F6 and decide whether to restrict the rider's account, and to advise the driver of the RydeHELP reporting path (and 995 if medical help is needed).

rejected_claims.reason: The rider-side request for no_action cannot be granted on this record: the rider's own timestamped message 'Say that again and I will punch you' [F4], in answer to the driver's 'Please do not smoke in the car' [F3], is intimidation aimed at the driver, so SAFE-1 requires escalation and no automatic ruling. The absence of a route deviation (0.0 km extra, F1) does not neutralise the safety clause.

The driver-side request for no_action is likewise unavailable: the driver's own complaint and statement [F6] describe a threat of violence by the rider, corroborated by the timestamped chat [F4][F5], so SAFE-1 mandates escalation rather than closing the case with no_action. The driver's good record [F8] is profile context and cannot decide the case.
